children: advanced sharply on Wednesday afternoon after the Federal Reserve delivered a 25-basis-point increase in its benchmark interest rate. The move lifted the DXY 0.67% to 100.21, its highest recorded level since July 31.

Investors responded immediately by adding exposure to the greenback. Higher U.S. rates improve the relative yield on dollar assets, prompting a swift rotation into the currency. The index now trades cleanly above its 20-day, 50-day, 100-day and 200-day moving averages, confirming a broad technical uptrend that had been building in recent sessions.

The Fed’s latest tightening step continues its effort to keep inflation in check while supporting a still-resilient labor market. Market participants interpreted the decision as a signal that policy will remain restrictive for longer than some had hoped, reinforcing demand for the dollar against a basket of major currencies.

With the DXY sitting at a multi-week high and all major moving averages aligned beneath price, traders are watching whether the breakout can hold. Sustained buying would keep pressure on foreign-exchange pairs and support dollar-denominated assets in the sessions ahead. The combination of a clear policy catalyst and improving technical structure has positioned the index as one of the day’s strongest performers.

title: Fed hike propels the dollar to its highest level since late July
